## What is measured

The corpus is [PRL-PRG/r-benchmarks](https://github.com/PRL-PRG/r-benchmarks):
118 programs in 8 suites (shootout, Are We Fast Yet, RealThing, SpeedTest,
riposte, mathkernel, R-benchmark-25, misc), characterised in *What Do R
Benchmarks Measure? Toward a Performance-Characterized Benchmark Suite for R*
(VMIL'26). Each program defines `execute(size)` and, optionally, an untimed
`setup()`. Timing, repetition and process management belong to the shared
harness, driven by the [bench](https://github.com/PRL-PRG/bench) framework.

## How R is built

- **Releases** are built from the CRAN source tarballs. **R-devel** is built
  from [r-devel/r-svn](https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn), one revision per night.
- On Linux, builds and runs happen in **container images pinned by digest**,
  so every release since 3.0.0 is built with the same compiler. On macOS and
  Windows a recorded toolchain manifest plays the same role.
- The default build is `-O2 -g` with OpenBLAS linked by name and all BLAS and
  OpenMP thread counts pinned to 1. `-g` only adds debug information and
  changes no instructions. Other [configurations](configs.qmd) change one
  thing each.

## How a run is measured

- Every benchmark runs in **5 separate R processes**, each doing 1 warm-up and
  4 measured iterations, in a fixed shuffled order, under `setarch -R`.
- Before a session the machine must pass `bench doctor` (governor, turbo,
  SMT, ASLR, THP, swap, load), and `bench denoise` is applied. Benchmark cores
  are isolated from the kernel scheduler.
- A **sentinel** benchmark checks that the machine behaves as it did before;
  see [Machines](machines.qmd).

## Statistics

- A benchmark's time on a run is the **geometric mean over processes** of
  each process's median iteration. Its interval is a 95% interval with the
  process as the unit of replication.
- A **speedup** is *time(A) / time(B)*: above 1× means B is faster. Speedups
  are only ever computed between runs on the **same machine**.
- The **baseline** (1×) is the R version shipped in the **newest Ubuntu LTS**,
  currently R `r BASELINE_VERSION` in Ubuntu `r UBUNTU_LTS$ubuntu[nrow(UBUNTU_LTS)]`:
  the R most Linux users get without adding CRAN's repository. The table of
  which R each LTS ships (`r paste0(UBUNTU_LTS$r, " in ", UBUNTU_LTS$ubuntu, collapse = ", ")`)
  is kept in `data/ubuntu-lts.csv`. Every build checks Ubuntu's release list
  for a newer LTS and reads the `r-base` version it shipped from Launchpad, so
  when a new LTS is released every speedup on the site is **rescaled to its R**
  at the next build. A machine that has not measured that release uses its oldest
  measured release instead.
- Suite-level numbers are **geometric means** over the benchmarks that every
  compared run could execute. The count is always shown, because old releases
  cannot run benchmarks that need newer R or packages.
- R-devel **change detection** flags a benchmark when it moves by more than
  2% and outside its interval relative to the previous seven good nights, and
  the next three nights confirm it.

## Profiles {#profiles}

A second pass records each benchmark 5 times with
`perf record --call-graph dwarf,32768` on the same `-O2 -g` build. Only samples
inside `execute()` are kept, using phase markers the harness prints. Each sample
is charged to the **innermost stack frame** a rule recognises, checked in this
order:

1. **Object rules:** frames in BLAS/LAPACK libraries are `native-blas`, and
   frames in a package's own shared object are `native-ffi`.
2. **Symbol rules:** a table of named interpreter functions (for example
   `bcEval` → interpreter, `R_findVar` → lookup, `Rf_duplicate` →
   mem-duplicate).
3. **Shape rule:** `do_*` and `ALT*` functions inside the interpreter are
   `primitives`, apart from the dispatch primitives (`UseMethod`,
   `NextMethod`, `standardGeneric`).

Samples no rule reaches are reported as **unattributed** and never hidden. A
run whose unattributed share exceeds 5% fails the quality gate. Profiles on
platforms without `perf` (macOS: samply) are marked *experimental* until their
category shares are shown to agree with perf.

```{r}
rs_table(data.frame(Category = CATEGORIES$category, Group = CATEGORIES$group,
                    `What it covers` = CATEGORIES$description, check.names = FALSE),
         pagination = FALSE, sortable = FALSE, columns = list(`What it covers` = colDef(minWidth = 360)))
```

## Data and licences

- Pipeline code: [PRL-PRG/speedR](https://github.com/PRL-PRG/speedR), MIT.
- Results: [PRL-PRG/speedR-results](https://github.com/PRL-PRG/speedR-results),
  **CC0**: raw bench reports, per-process samples and per-benchmark profiles
